method: TWO KINDS OF ROW, and they are labelled. Repetitions 0, 1, 3, 4, 6, 9, 10 and 11 are TRANSCRIBED from the frame-strip readings recorded in gracious-blackburn spikes/poc-output/coach/video-clips/manifest.json and video-clips-v2/manifest.json. Repetitions 2, 5, 7 and 8 are A FRESH LOOK by the video-readiness lane on 2026-09-02: frames selected by TIMESTAMP with no seek at all, labelled with the true container PTS, read in the front view and confirmed in the side view where it mattered, and magnified to a top-crop wherever a ball was near the frame edge. Every row says which it is.

windowSource.note: The windows below are that file's own. If the alignment tooling moves them, loading refuses this whole annotation rather than reattaching a person's judgement to different footage.

repetitions.evidence: THE REPETITION THIS CONDITION EXISTS FOR. The clip lane's manifest records it verbatim: 'best warp distance in the set (0.02369) and NO BALL IS PRESENT. A frame strip across the whole window shows the athlete standing and gesturing.' Rejected on sight after scoring best of twelve on the whole-curve scoring and rank 1 of 8 drills on both scorings.

Cut as the 'catch' clip for section 1 of the coach page, so its catch was watched frame by frame in both views. A ball at the anchored moment, and not for the whole 2.6 s window.

A FRESH LOOK by the video-readiness lane, 2026-09-02. Front view, frames selected by timestamp and read at two magnifications. She catches at 11.200-11.400 with the ball plainly in her hands. The ball then leaves the TOP of the frame at 11.633 — a top-crop across 11.600 to 12.133 shows it at the edge in 11.600 and gone in every frame after. The anchor is 11.733 and the peak 12.100, so NO BALL IS IN FRAME across the anchored span. This is not a gesture: it is a real catch whose anchor lands after the ball has left the picture.

The manifest calls it a 'genuine catch', rejected only because 'its two rankings disagree (margin -0.006) and three clips is enough for a page'. A catch was seen; the whole window was not commented on.
Cut as the rep04 clip for the coach page, so its moment was watched frame by frame in both views before the cut.

A FRESH LOOK by the video-readiness lane, 2026-09-02. Front view. She waits with hands up and empty from 14.000 to 14.750, and the ball descends into frame at 14.875 — inside the anchored span of 14.467 to 14.900, with 25 ms to spare. Confirmed in the side view. A real catch whose window ends as the ball arrives.

'genuine catch, rankings disagree (margin -0.003), not needed'. A catch was seen. Note that this repetition has the BEST informative warp distance in the set at 0.00435, five times better than the no-ball repetition.

A FRESH LOOK by the video-readiness lane, 2026-09-02. Front view, top-crop across 17.133 to 17.600 at full resolution. She catches at 16.800-17.000, then tosses: the ball is motion-blurred but UNAMBIGUOUS at 17.133, 17.167 and at the anchor itself, 17.200, and is half out of frame by 17.233 and gone by 17.267. At 230 px wide this blur read as ambiguous and the magnified crop settled it, which is why the close look is part of the method rather than an extra.

A FRESH LOOK by the video-readiness lane, 2026-09-02. Front view, every frame of the window at two magnifications plus a top-crop across 18.067 to 18.333. She stands, talks and gestures with her hands clasped at her chest. NO BALL ANYWHERE in the picture at any point in the window. The same shape as repetition 0, and the second gesture stretch the alignment accepted as a repetition.

'genuine catch, but it runs to 25.0 s, close to the point where the front camera goes dark at 25.7 s, and the framing changes at its end'. A catch was seen; the rejection is about the camera rather than the ball.

note: THREE of twelve repetitions have no ball in frame at the anchored moment, and for TWO different reasons. Repetitions 0 and 8 are gesture stretches with no ball anywhere in the window. Repetition 2 is a REAL CATCH whose anchor lands 0.1 s after the ball has left the top of the frame. Repetitions 5 and 7 pass by 25 ms and by one frame respectively. Nothing here is null any longer.
seekWarning: WITHDRAWN AND REPLACED, 2026-09-02. An earlier version of this field blamed FAST SEEK (`-ss` before `-i`) on the variable-rate side camera, and said the clip manifests used that method. THAT BLAME IS NOT SUPPORTED and it impugned a method that is fine. Measured: asked for a single frame at 17.030, fast seek, `-copyts` accurate seek and `select` by timestamp ALL return the identical source frame, pts 17.0599 (the first frame at or after the request), matched against the source at a difference of 0.663 against a next rival of 3.324. Seeking is not the fault. WHAT IS ESTABLISHED is narrower: a label computed as a FIXED OFFSET plus the output timestamp, inside a filter chain that RESAMPLES (`fps=`) and TILES, can diverge from the frames it is printed on — and one such chain asked for 9.733 s produced frames whose true timestamps ran 12.000 to 14.200. The content was real footage and the labels were fiction, which is the worst shape a mislabelling can take. SO: label with the TRUE container PTS (`%{pts\:hms}` with no offset), select by timestamp rather than seeking when a window matters, and if a reading is consequential, MATCH THE FRAME BACK against the source rather than trusting any label. Every reading in this file was taken that way.
